description: The page's last screen: how to reach the business (phone first), when it's open, where it works, a final trust reminder (license, founding year, rating) and a brand sign-off. For trades it's a working contact card, not a sitemap.
queries: footer with contact details and locations
footer with large call to action and phone number
local shop footer with address, opening hours and map

references.layout: A wordmark (~150px) spanning the full width at the top, a hairline beneath it, then a grid: two office columns (city name with live local time and a weather icon, address, email) and, behind a vertical hairline on the right, a newsletter signup. Tiny utility text is pinned to the bottom corners.
references.type: Wordmark neo-grotesk regular ~150px with tight tracking; body sans ~8px; times in monospace ('09 09 (GMT-4)').
references.color: White ~#FFFFFF and black ~#000000; emails in grey ~#8A8A8A.
details: Each city shows its live local time and a weather glyph
The wordmark is sized to exactly fill the width
A thin vertical rule separates contact info from signup
A tiny tagline at bottom-left ('Mother Design has a soul')
references.why_it_works: A massive wordmark over a functional grid is a staple of premium footers, and the live time makes the offices feel open and alive.
references.trade_adaptation: Business name across the full width; under it a live 'Open now · closes 6pm' status beside the address, a 24/7 emergency line and the service-area towns.

references.layout: A dense grid on white: tagline top-left, three nav columns, a secure-payments block on the right and a scrolling marquee of industries. Then a contact row: a B&W photo on the left; head office with a 'Direction on Google' link, email, hotline, office hours and an 'Operating across' list; and a dotted world map with location pins on the right. A giant dot-matrix wordmark runs along the very bottom.
references.type: Labels monospace caps ~7px tracked; values sans ~10px; marquee ~18px light grey; dot-matrix wordmark ~70px.
references.color: White ~#FFFFFF; text ~#111111; labels ~#777777; marquee ~#C8C8C8; map dots ~#D0D0D0 with navy pins ~#1A2A6C.
details: 'Direction on Google' with a turn-arrow glyph sits right under the address
Hours and hotline each get their own labelled cell
A dotted map with pins shows where the company works
Monospace micro-labels ('HEAD OFFICE', 'HOTLINE', 'OFFICE HOURS') structure the dense information
references.why_it_works: It shows how to fit everything a local customer needs (address, directions, phone, hours, coverage) into an orderly grid.
references.trade_adaptation: Swap the world map for a dotted county map with pins on service towns; 'HOTLINE' becomes '24/7 EMERGENCY'; use a B&W photo of the shop or yard.

references.layout: Three centred columns with all-caps headings, 'CONTACT', 'OPENING HOURS' and 'FIND US', each with centred caps details beneath (the hours include a full holiday schedule) and an 'I NEED A REAL MAP →' link. Below sits a hand-drawn line illustration with curved text, and a tiny monospace copyright and credit in the bottom corners.
references.type: Headings condensed sans caps ~18px; details ~8px caps; illustration caption in curved caps.
details: Holiday hours spelled out line by line
Link copy with humour: 'I NEED A REAL MAP →'
A hand-drawn illustration with a curved tagline gives a signature sign-off
Just three headings, exactly what a local customer looks for
references.why_it_works: It answers the three local-business questions (how do I reach you, when, where) in a warm, branded way.
references.trade_adaptation: 'CALL / HOURS / SERVICE AREA' columns with emergency and holiday hours, and a line drawing of a house or van with the curved tagline 'Keeping Tulsa warm since 1987'.

references.layout: A red outer frame (~8px margin) around a cream inner card. Inside: a chunky serif wordmark with a small illustration on the left, nav columns in the middle, an embedded playlist card on the right, and a 'VISIT US' tag with two addresses and email/social at bottom-left. Below the card, on the red: an illustrated mascot with a 'FOLLOW US ON THE GRAM' speech bubble, a strip of square photos and a tiny copyright bar.
references.type: Wordmark soft display serif ~40px; labels monospace caps ~7px inside a dark tag; body ~9px.
references.color: Frame ~#C8341A; card ~#F3E9DD; wordmark and text ~#4A1F14; tag ~#4A1F14 with cream text.
details: A card inside a coloured frame
A small dark label tag ('VISIT US') above the addresses
A strip of real shop and community photos
An illustrated mascot with a speech bubble
references.why_it_works: A local-shop footer full of personality and real photos; the frame makes it feel like a printed menu.
references.trade_adaptation: Replace the playlist with a 'Recent jobs' photo strip; tag 'COME SEE THE SHOWROOM' or 'NOW SERVING'; the mascot can be an illustration of the van. Rustic and friendly styles.

references.layout: Top area: a friendly one-liner and an outlined email field with a small green submit button on the left; three link columns on the right, behind a dotted vertical rule; dotted horizontal rules; a legal line. Bottom: an enormous wavy display wordmark spanning the full width.
references.type: Body in a typewriter-like serif ~11px; wordmark heavy, wobbly display face ~150px.
references.color: Peach ~#F6E3D3; text and wordmark olive ~#3D4430; submit button lime ~#B6E36A.
details: Dotted rules instead of solid hairlines
The wordmark is in a characterful display face, so the footer becomes the brand moment
Friendly copy: 'Friends let friends know about fresh products and content.'
references.why_it_works: A strong brand finish with a warm palette and characterful type; easy to template with any display face.
references.trade_adaptation: A painter or landscaper: the business name huge in a characterful serif, an earthy palette, and 'Neighbours tell neighbours' above a phone or email field.

references.layout: Six centred blocks in a 3×2 grid, each with a very widely letter-spaced caps label over short caps content. Hand-drawn ovals loop around the Location and Contact blocks. A script wordmark is centred below, and two black pill buttons flank a legal line.
references.type: Monospace caps ~9px; labels with extremely wide tracking; wordmark italic script ~36px.
details: Hand-drawn ovals circle the two most important blocks
Ultra-wide tracked labels act as decoration
A script wordmark as the sign-off
references.why_it_works: It shows how a hand-drawn emphasis mark can steer attention to the contact info inside an otherwise uniform grid.
references.trade_adaptation: Circle the phone number and service area with a marker-style oval. Suits playful cleaning or pest-control brands.

references.layout: Two halves split by a vertical hairline, on warm off-white with faint grid lines in the margins. Left: logo, an 'Established in 1988…' paragraph, the registered office address, a regulatory line and a row of three accreditation badges including a review score. Right: two link columns, a policies list, and a newsletter field with a button. Bottom bar: copyright with registration numbers, and social icons.
references.color: Off-white ~#FBF8F4; text ~#1F2A33; teal accent ~#1F7A7A; input fill ~#DFF1F1 with a dashed border.
details: The blurb opens with the founding year
Regulatory and registration numbers appear in the footer as trust
Accreditation badges and the review score are repeated in the footer
Dashed-outline inputs and buttons match the rest of the site
references.why_it_works: The footer becomes a final trust checkpoint (year, license, badges, rating) without looking cluttered.
references.trade_adaptation: 'Family-owned since 1988', 'Licensed & insured · Lic. #ROC-123456', BBB and manufacturer badges and the Google rating, plus service links, with a quote-request field instead of a newsletter.

references.layout: Columns topped with hairlines. The brand name sits on the left; then email and phone; then two location columns, each with name, address and hours ('Tuesday – Saturday, 11am – 6pm') plus a 'Book an Appointment' or 'Learn More' link. A second tier has the newsletter on the left and link columns on the right; copyright and credit sit at the bottom.
details: Hours sit directly under each address
Each location has its own action link ('Book an Appointment')
One ink colour (maroon) for everything, rules included
references.why_it_works: The cleanest multi-location format, and the single ink colour makes it feel designed.
references.trade_adaptation: 'Showroom' and 'Shop & warehouse' columns with hours and 'Book a design visit'; the ink colour is the brand accent.

references.layout: A dark CTA band with a two-line serif headline, a one-line prompt and a pill button, crossed by a thick gradient ribbon. Below it a light footer: a stacked logo on the left, a large caps link list (~16px) in the middle, and a big serif 'Sign up to our newsletter' with a pill input and attached button on the right.
references.type: Headline serif ~36px; links caps grotesk ~16px; newsletter heading serif ~28px.
references.color: CTA band chocolate ~#3A1A12; button and accent lime ~#E6F75A; footer ~#E9E7E4; text ~#3A1A12.
details: A final CTA band comes directly before the footer
Footer links are set large (~16px) rather than as tiny columns
Input and button merged into one pill
references.why_it_works: It ends the page with one clear action and large, easy-to-tap links.
references.trade_adaptation: A 'Need it fixed today? / Call (555) 123-4567' band, then large links: Services · Service area · Reviews · Financing.

references.layout: A bento of rounded blocks on black. Top: a yellow newsletter block and a blue support block. Middle: a full-width marquee row of alternating coloured pills with a huge condensed 'GET SLUSH' and a logo circle. Bottom: 2×2 white social-icon tiles on the left, and a green block with a condensed italic slogan, a link list and the legal line.
references.type: Condensed heavy grotesk caps ~60px in the marquee; slogan condensed italic ~22px; links caps ~11px.
references.color: Black ~#000000 gutters; blocks yellow ~#FFD84D, blue ~#3E8BFF, orange ~#FF5A1F, green ~#43D693, purple ~#5A3FE0; white tiles.
details: Each block is a different saturated colour, all with the same ~16px radius
Giant social icons on white tiles
A marquee of the brand name as the sign-off
references.why_it_works: A loud, energetic footer for a bold style; the blocks keep dense content organised.
references.trade_adaptation: A bold brand (junk removal, pest control, garage doors): blocks for 'Call now', 'Book online' and 'Service area', with a marquee of the business name.

references.layout: A gradient CTA band ('call to get the full picture') with a 'CALL (866) 951-7154' button, then a dark footer with four link columns and a right column that reads 'Need help deciding…? Give us a call at' followed by the phone number in large bold type (~18px), social icons, and centred legal links.
references.type: Sans; column headings caps ~10px; phone number ~18px semibold.
references.color: Band gradient from navy ~#1F1640 to red ~#D9534F; footer ~#2D333F; text ~#D5D8DE; phone number ~#FFFFFF.
details: The phone number is the largest text in the footer
The phone number appears inside the button label itself ('CALL (866) …')
A friendly lead-in sentence comes before the number
references.why_it_works: For call-driven businesses the phone number should be the hero of the footer, and this shows that hierarchy.
references.trade_adaptation: For every trade: 'Not sure what you need? Give us a call' with a big tap-to-call number, plus an emergency line if they work 24/7.

references.layout: A single slim footer: a small logo and a one-line origin note on the left; two short link groups ('Sitemap', 'Email') on the right; a hairline; then a bottom line with '©2026 ISO Meet. Made with ♥ in Texas' on the left and 'Follow us' with one icon on the right.
details: 'Made with ♥ in Texas' puts local pride in the legal line
An origin note: 'built by people who've lived it'
Only what's needed, nothing more
references.why_it_works: A good model for secondary pages or very small businesses, and the local-pride line is a small human touch.
references.trade_adaptation: '© 2026 Henderson Plumbing · Family-owned in Boise since 1994 · Lic. #PL-1234'.

takeaways: For a trade, the footer's job is phone, hours and service area. Give each a labelled, prominent cell, and make the phone number the largest text.
Put a directions link under the address and hours under each location, and spell out emergency and holiday hours.
Finish on a brand moment: a full-width wordmark or one characterful display word.
Repeat trust in the footer: founding year, license number, a couple of flattened badges and the rating.
Use one ink colour or one accent, and prefer hairlines or dotted rules to boxes.
Place a final CTA band ('Call now' / 'Get a free quote') directly above the footer.
Add one human line or mark ('Family-owned in X since Y', a local illustration, a mascot).
avoid: SaaS mega-footers with 5-6 columns of product and resource links (Ramp, Notion, Slack)
App-store badges, cookie-preference toggles and language selectors on a local trade site
A newsletter signup as the main footer action instead of call or quote
A generic row of social icons as the only contact method
Tiny grey-on-grey text for the phone number and address
